items.name: upload.inline
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.4 · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → app_llm_facade → host_upload_service → R2
items.summary: Single-shot upload — bundle base64-encodes the file and posts it inline in the RPC body. Best for payloads ≤ 8 MiB already in memory: one round-trip vs three for the negotiate/confirm flow. The host validates MIME + purpose against `upload_grant`, decodes, writes to R2 under a per-(user, App) prefix, and returns a short-lived download URL.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.

items.signature: anna.upload.inline(args: {filename: string, mime_type: string, content_b64: string, purpose?: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{r2_key, mime_type, bytes_size, download_url, expires_in}>

params.name: filename
params.summary: Human-readable filename. Used in the R2 object path and exposed in the download `Content-Disposition` for the bytes when fetched.

params.name: mime_type
params.summary: Wire MIME type of the payload. Must pass the host denylist (SVG is forced to attachment, executables are rejected). The per-user MIME allowlist was removed — any non-blocked type is accepted, Office formats included.
notes: Allowlist failure → `APP_PROVIDER_ERROR` (HTTP 400 underneath) with the `host_upload_service` reason verbatim — typically `MIME_REJECTED`.
Glob wildcards (`image/*`) in the grant are honoured.

params.name: content_b64
params.summary: Base64-encoded bytes of the file. Inline payload after decode must be ≤ `upload_grant.maxFileBytes` (default **20 MiB**).
notes: Wire size ≈ 1.33× raw bytes. A 15 MiB file becomes ~20 MiB on the wire — if you regularly approach the cap, use `upload.negotiate`+`confirm` instead to skip the encode overhead.
Browsers: never use `btoa(String.fromCharCode(...))` on multi-MiB buffers — it allocates a UTF-16 intermediate. Prefer `FileReader.readAsDataURL` + slice off the prefix.

params.name: purpose
params.summary: Why the file is being uploaded — used for billing categorisation and to scope `upload_grant.allowedPurposes`. Allowed values: `image_input`, `image_reference`, `user_artifact`.
notes: Outside the host's set → `APP_PROVIDER_ERROR` with reason `PURPOSE_REJECTED` (HTTP 403 underneath).
If `upload_grant.allowedPurposes` is configured, the value must additionally appear in that allowlist.
Choose `image_input` when you plan to feed the result to `image.edit`/`image.generate` so billing rows correlate.

returns.type: { r2_key: string, mime_type: string, bytes_size: int, download_url: string, expires_in: int }
returns.desc:
• `r2_key` — opaque storage handle (`exec-uploads/<env>/<user_uuid>/<tool_id>/<invoke_id>/<purpose>/<file>`). **Persist this, not `download_url`.**
• `mime_type` — server-canonicalised MIME (may differ from the requested value if SVG was forced to attachment, etc.).
• `bytes_size` — actual decoded size.
• `download_url` — presigned R2 GET, TTL = `expires_in` seconds (~30 min). Re-mint by calling `upload.confirm` with the saved `r2_key`.

errors.name: APP_PROVIDER_ERROR
errors.desc: MIME or purpose rejected, too-large after decode, R2 PUT failure, or any other `host_upload_service.HostUploadError`. Mapped from `APP_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR` (-32003) with the underlying reason preserved in `message` (and HTTP status hinted by it: 400 for `MIME_REJECTED`/`TOO_LARGE`/`INVALID_REQUEST`, 403 for `PURPOSE_REJECTED`, 502 otherwise).

limitations: Decoded payload cap is `upload_grant.maxFileBytes` (default 20 MiB). Hard ceiling for `inline` in practice is ~8 MiB raw / ~10 MiB wire because larger postMessages stutter the iframe → host channel.
Synchronous. No progress events, no resume on partial failure — for multi-MB payloads on slow networks use `upload.negotiate`+`confirm` so the bytes flow directly to R2 with native PUT progress.
`download_url` expires (~30 min). Always persist `r2_key`; re-mint URLs through `upload.confirm`.
MIME canonicalisation: requesting `image/svg+xml` may return `application/octet-stream` (SVG forced to attachment to prevent active content). Plan your renderer accordingly.
No de-duplication. Uploading the same bytes twice produces two distinct `r2_key`s and counts against quota twice.

items.name: upload.negotiate
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.4 · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0
items.summary: Step 1/2 of the large-file flow. Validates MIME + purpose against `upload_grant`, mints a presigned R2 PUT URL (5-minute TTL), and returns the `r2_key` the bundle should remember. Does **not** count against the file quota — that's charged on `upload.confirm`.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.

items.signature: anna.upload.negotiate(args: {filename: string, mime_type: string, purpose?: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{r2_key, put_url, expires_in, headers}>

params.name: filename
params.summary: Human-readable filename. Used in the R2 object path.

params.name: mime_type
params.summary: Final MIME of the PUT body. Validated against the host denylist only (MIME allowlist removed).
notes: **The browser MUST send the exact same `Content-Type` header on the PUT** — R2 rejects mismatches with HTTP 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch.

params.name: purpose
params.summary: One of `image_input`, `image_reference`, `user_artifact` — additionally constrained by `upload_grant.allowedPurposes` if set. Outside the set → `APP_PROVIDER_ERROR` `PURPOSE_REJECTED`.

returns.type: { r2_key: string, put_url: string, expires_in: int, headers: Record<string,string> }
returns.desc:
• `r2_key` — durable storage handle. **Save this immediately** — without it the post-PUT object is unreachable.
• `put_url` — presigned PUT URL, TTL = `expires_in` (default ~300 s). PUT bytes here directly from the browser; no auth header needed (it's signed in).
• `headers` — additional headers the browser MUST send on the PUT (e.g. `Content-Type`, sometimes `x-amz-meta-*`). Some are required for the signature to validate; copy verbatim.

errors.name: APP_PROVIDER_ERROR
errors.desc: MIME or purpose rejected, or R2 signing failure (rare; surfaces as HTTP 502 underneath).

limitations: PUT URL TTL is ~5 min. Slow uploads on flaky networks can race the expiry; renegotiate rather than retrying the same `put_url`.
Browser CORS: R2 must allow PUT from the iframe origin. Anna Apps' R2 bucket is preconfigured for this; if you self-host, mirror the CORS rules in `docs/design/`.
Negotiate is free — but if you negotiate-without-confirm repeatedly, the orphan R2 objects can still appear in the bucket (lifecycle policy reaps them). Don't rely on that for cleanup.

No `size_bytes` validation at negotiate time. A file larger than `upload_grant.maxFileBytes` will succeed at PUT but fail at `upload.confirm` with `TOO_LARGE` after HEAD. Pre-check `file.size` in the bundle to fail fast.

items.name: upload.confirm
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.4 · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → app_llm_facade → host_upload_service (HEAD R2)
items.summary: Step 2/2 of the large-file flow. The host HEADs the R2 object to verify the PUT actually landed, validates size against `upload_grant.maxFileBytes`, records the upload (charging the file quota), and returns the canonical `download_url`. Idempotent on success — repeated calls re-mint the URL without double-charging.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.

items.signature: anna.upload.confirm(args: {r2_key: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{r2_key, mime_type, bytes_size, download_url, expires_in}>

params.name: r2_key
params.summary: Storage handle returned by `upload.negotiate` (or a prior `upload.inline`/`upload.confirm`).
notes: Used both to locate the R2 object and to derive `expected_invoke_id` for cross-check: the host parses position 4 of the slash-split path and rejects mismatches with `APP_PROVIDER_ERROR` `NOT_FOUND`.

returns.type: { r2_key: string, mime_type: string, bytes_size: int, download_url: string, expires_in: int }
returns.desc: Same shape as `upload.inline` return. Use this method to mint a **fresh** `download_url` whenever the old one expires — pass the persisted `r2_key` and get a new presigned GET (~30 min TTL).

errors.name: APP_PROVIDER_ERROR
errors.desc: Either `NOT_FOUND` (HTTP 404 underneath — the PUT never happened, expired, or the key was tampered with), `TOO_LARGE` (PUT'd bytes exceed `maxFileBytes`), or any `host_upload_service.HostUploadError` (HTTP 502 underneath).

limitations: Confirm charges the per-day file quota on first call for a given `r2_key`. Subsequent confirms on the same key are idempotent and free, but a fresh negotiate→confirm cycle does count.
No automatic background re-confirm. Your app must call `upload.confirm` again any time the cached `download_url` is older than `expires_in`.
The HEAD-then-record sequence is not transactional. If the host crashes between HEAD and record, you may need to call `upload.confirm` again — it's safe.
`r2_key` is opaque but **not** secret to other Apps owned by the same user; do not embed credentials in the filename portion of the negotiate request.
